Get started with zugrpc

zugrpc.Rmd
library(zugrpc)

gRPC is how many services talk to each other, Spark Connect among them. It runs only over HTTP/2 and carries its status in HTTP trailers, which the usual R HTTP clients do not expose. zugrpc speaks the gRPC wire protocol on top of zuhttp’s HTTP/2. You bring the request message, encoded with zuproto, and get back the response message, its metadata and its status. Calls can be unary or server-streaming.

Open a channel

A channel holds the connection to one server. An http:// URL is cleartext HTTP/2, for a local server. An https:// URL negotiates HTTP/2 over TLS.

ch <- grpc_channel("http://localhost:15002")

ch <- grpc_channel(
  "https://spark.example.org:443",
  tls = zuhttp::zu_tls(ca_file = NULL),
  headers = c(authorization = "Bearer ..."),
  keepalive = grpc_keepalive(time = 60, timeout = 20),
  max_message = 128 * 1024^2
)

Make a unary call

A unary call sends one request message and returns one response message. The request is a raw vector, typically from zuproto::proto_encode(). The deadline is in seconds, or an absolute POSIXct.

# Open: whether grpc_call() returns a plain list or an S3 object with accessors
res <- grpc_call(
  ch, "/spark.connect.SparkConnectService/AnalyzePlan",
  request = req_bytes,
  metadata = c("x-user-agent" = "zuspark"),
  deadline = 30
)
res$message
res$headers
res$trailers
res$status

Stream the responses

A server-streaming call returns a stream. Each $next_message() returns one response message, and NULL at the end. The server only sends more as you read.

st <- grpc_stream(
  ch, "/spark.connect.SparkConnectService/ExecutePlan",
  request = req_bytes, deadline = 600
)
st$headers()
# Open: should $next_message() take a timeout of its own, or is the call
# deadline enough?
while (!is.null(m <- st$next_message())) {
  zuproto::proto_decode(m, type, pool)
}
st$trailers()
st$status()

Cancel a stream you no longer need. A second cancel does nothing.

st$cancel()

Handle errors

A call that ends with a non-OK status raises a zugrpc_error_status condition. Its class also carries the status, so you can catch one code. The details field holds the decoded google.rpc.Status.

tryCatch(
  grpc_call(ch, "/spark.connect.SparkConnectService/AnalyzePlan",
            request = req_bytes),
  zugrpc_error_unavailable = function(cnd) {
    cnd$message
  },
  zugrpc_error_status = function(cnd) {
    cnd$details
  }
)

grpc_status_codes()

Close and inspect

Closing a channel cancels its open streams. zugrpc_info() reports the zuhttp version, whether it offers HTTP/2 and its TLS backend.

grpc_close(ch)
zugrpc_info()
